To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have shown that PZT films are very promising for microactuators.

the transverse piezo coefficient e31,f of PZT films is of the order of -18 C/m2 and can be measured with the setup developed in this work, that the piezoelectricty of the PZT films does not degrade under high electric fields and high frequency cycling and that the leakage current increases toward the end of a long-term test.

the piezoelectic stress in thin film PZT cantilevers can be measured with an accuracy of 1.5%, that the transverse piezoresponse is a reliable measure of the piezocapacitive stress, and that the piezocoupling coefficient e31,f is not a constant, but a function of the applied field and of the history of the polarization of the film, which is related to its ferroelectric properties.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization and reliability of piezoelectrics for MEMS applications.
the development of a novel piezoelectric actuator technology for MEMS applications, based on sol-gel derived lead zirconate titanate thin films.
the development and application of piezoelectrical thin films.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
sol-gel PZT thin-films are promising for MEMS applications.
the PZT sol-gel thin film material is suitable for actuator applications in microelectronics.
the PZT thin film is a very promising material for actuator applications in microelectromechanics.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the converse piezoelectric effect in PZT thin film actuators is very robust and can be used for a variety of MEMS applications.
the transverse piezoresponse of PZT is a good candidate for the actuation of MEMS.
we have developed a method to characterize the transverse piezo coefficient e31,f of PZT films.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the piezoelectrics are not a limiting factor for the reliability of PZT-based microactuators.
PZT is a promising candidate for actuating MEMS, provided the device is designed for the high leakage that will occur at high field.
the converse effect is a very robust property of piezoelectrics and can be used for reliable actuation of MEMS structures.
